date_note: The page gives only its own publication day (23 November); it says users were notified that day.
title: European Commission says cyberattack disrupted EU Academy platform and leaked user data
summary: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said names and email addresses were among the data taken from EU Academy; the scale is under investigation (AP). AP says the Commission first detected incidents on 22 October. Regnier declined to say whether it is under control; BleepingComputer reports the Commission has not attributed the attack or received a ransom demand. Euronews, citing two sources, reports it suspects a China-backed actor.
plain: The European Commission says an attack disrupted its EU Academy learning platform; its spokesperson says names and email addresses were among the stolen data and the extent is still being investigated.
exec: The Commission says user data from an EU platform leaked; the report ties it to an earlier campaign against Commission systems.
action: The EU Academy site advises users to be alert to suspicious or unsolicited emails and messages and not to share personal information with anyone who contacts them about the site.

validation.note: AP, BleepingComputer, Security Affairs, Shorouk News, Voria.gr, Mikrometoxos.gr and O Liberal (Estadão) each relay the Commission spokesperson's statement that EU Academy was hit; the Commission's own page could not be loaded.
